result.topic_en: The upright top part concludes an argument (Art. 5, citing Art. 12) that z is a continuous function of w on the surface T because dz/dw does not depend on the direction of displacement. Most of the page is upside down: heavily corrected, largely illegible draft passages that refer to the geometric representation of complex quantities, to Art. 3 and to a work of 1832.

methods.what: A function is analytic (continuous complex function) if its derivative is independent of the direction of displacement; by Art. 12 it then forms a continuous function of the complex variable on T
